title: LSL open_timeout follow-up of M6-14: shorter configurable open limit + fast reconnect (continuous resolver)
notes: Follow-up of M6-14 (reconnect about 6.3 s, blamed on the 5 s open_timeout). LSLMapping.open_timeout_s (default 1.0 s, was fixed 5 s; --open-timeout; collector open_timeout_s); start retries a timed-out open until the resolve timeout. Measurement experiments/2026-11-14-m6-16-lsl-open-timeout (background CPU class): healthy open p50 11.5 ms; stale open waits the full limit; a shorter open_timeout alone did NOT change the reconnect (6.2-6.8 s in 10/12 restarts at 5/2/1/0.5 s). Cause: one-shot resolve(timeout 0.5 s) right after a loss blocks about 5.5 s on Windows (contradicts the M6-14 note). Fix: reopen uses a pylsl ContinuousResolver, prefers a new uid over stale info, old uid after 2 s (LSLMapping.reconnect_resolver continuous / oneshot). Reconnect after a 1.5 s outage 2.42 s in 6/6 runs; max loop step 21.0-21.3 ms (M6-14 holds). Tests tests/test_lsl_open_timeout.py (7, incl. real-LSL restart < 4.5 s); test_lsl_reconnect.py unchanged and passing.
